title: GCSE Physics Practice Paper 1
summary: Foundation and crossover · grades 1 to 5 · 24 questions · 36 min

questions.question: What is the unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules (J). The watt is the unit of power, the newton of force and the volt of potential difference.

questions.question: A trolley of mass 4 kg moves at 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy $= \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 5^2 = 50$ J.

questions.question: Which of these reduces unwanted energy transfers in a machine with moving parts?
questions.explanation: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, so less energy is wasted by heating.

questions.question: How should an ammeter be connected to measure the current in a lamp?
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series so that the same current flows through it and the lamp. A voltmeter is the meter connected in parallel.

questions.question: The potential difference across a resistor is 9 V and the current in it is 0.5 A. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance $= \frac{V}{I} = \frac{9}{0.5} = 18\ \Omega$.

questions.question: Which statement describes the mains electricity supply in the UK?
options: About 12 V, alternating current at 50 Hz
About 230 V, alternating current at 50 Hz
About 50 V, alternating current at 230 Hz
questions.explanation: UK mains is an alternating current supply with a potential difference of about 230 V and a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.question: An appliance has a power of 920 W and runs on a 230 V supply. Which fuse is the most suitable?
questions.explanation: Current is power divided by potential difference: 920 divided by 230 = 4 A. The fuse should be rated just above the normal current, so 5 A is the best choice.

questions.question: In which state of matter are the particles close together in a regular pattern?
questions.explanation: In a solid the particles are close together in a regular arrangement and vibrate about fixed positions.

questions.question: A metal has a density of $8\ \text{g/cm}^3$. What is the mass of $50\ \text{cm}^3$ of the metal?
questions.explanation: Mass $=$ density $\times$ volume $= 8 \times 50 = 400$ g.

questions.question: A neutral atom has 6 protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation: A neutral atom has no overall charge, so the number of negative electrons equals the number of positive protons: 6.

questions.question: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are the least penetrating: they are stopped by paper, skin or a few centimetres of air.

questions.question: A nucleus emits an alpha particle. How do its mass number and atomic number change?
options: Mass number down by 2, atomic number down by 4
Mass number unchanged, atomic number up by 1
Mass number down by 4, atomic number down by 2
Mass number down by 4, atomic number unchanged
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons. Losing it reduces the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2.

questions.question: What is the unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). The joule is the unit of energy, the pascal of pressure and the kilogram of mass.

questions.question: A box is pulled to the right with a force of 30 N. Friction of 12 N acts to the left. What is the resultant force?
questions.explanation: The forces act in opposite directions, so subtract: 30 minus 12 = 18 N, in the direction of the larger force, to the right.

questions.question: What is the unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second, so its unit is metres per second per second, $\text{m/s}^2$.

questions.question: A cyclist travels at a steady 15 m/s for 40 s. How far does the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Distance is speed multiplied by time: 15 times 40 = 600 m.

questions.question: Which statement is Newton's third law?
options: When two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal in size and opposite in direction
An object stays at rest unless a resultant force acts on it
Force equals mass multiplied by acceleration
questions.explanation: Newton's third law says that when two objects interact, they exert equal and opposite forces on each other.

questions.question: A driver's thinking distance is 12 m and the braking distance is 38 m. What is the stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is thinking distance plus braking distance: 12 + 38 = 50 m.

questions.question: A car of mass 900 kg travels at 10 m/s. What is its momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity: 900 times 10 = 9000 kg m/s.

questions.question: What is the amplitude of a wave?
options: The number of waves passing a point each second
The distance from one peak to the next
The time for one complete wave
The maximum displacement of a point on the wave from its rest position
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the undisturbed position. The distance between peaks is the wavelength, and waves per second is the frequency.

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 200 Hz and a wavelength of 1.7 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Wave speed is frequency multiplied by wavelength: 200 times 1.7 = 340 m/s.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelength and the lowest frequency. Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

questions.question: In which direction do magnetic field lines point around a bar magnet?
options: In circles that never touch the poles
questions.explanation: Field lines show the direction of the force on a north pole, so they point away from the magnet's north pole and towards its south pole.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.explanation: Our solar system is part of the Milky Way galaxy, which contains hundreds of billions of stars.
